newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH 1YR MONEY MARKET RATES JUMP ON CROWN TURMOIL.
newsitem.headline: CZECH 1YR MONEY MARKET RATES JUMP ON CROWN TURMOIL.

text.p: Czech one-year money market rates rose strongly on Thursday in response to a tumultuous morning which saw the Czech crown dive against its mark/dollar basket and the Czech central bank intervene to prop it up.

Local dealers said that one-year rates had risen by nearly a percentage point since the open to around 12.60/12.90 and were pushing 13 percent. The central bank said there would be no repo operations on Thursday.

The Czech crown fell to -5.0 percent against its mark/dollar basket prompting direct intervention from the Czech National Bank (CNB). The intervention pulled the crown back up to around -3.3 percent against the basket mid-point.
One local crown money market dealer said the interbank market was nervous and awaiting direction from the central bank through a statement.
"They (the CNB) must say someting to calm down the market because right now the market is very nervous and nobody knows where we are going," he said.
